title: Number sets ℕ ℤ ℚ ℝ
examples: What is the difference between integers and rational numbers?
Can you show me an example of a number that is in the rational numbers but not in the integers?
How do I know if a decimal will repeat forever?

explain.say: Today we are looking at different number sets. We will learn about natural numbers, integers, and rational numbers. These sets help us classify all types of numbers.

draw.text: Number sets ℕ ℤ ℚ ℝ

explain.say: The natural numbers are the counting numbers you use every day. These numbers start at one and go up by one. For example, three, five, and twenty are natural numbers.
Integers include the natural numbers and zero, plus the negative counting numbers. Think of them as whole numbers, positive or negative. For example, zero, four, and negative two are integers.
Rational numbers are numbers that can be written as a fraction of two integers. This includes all terminating and recurring decimals. For example, one half, or zero point five, is a rational number.

Now let us look at decimals. Some decimals stop, which we call terminating. For example, two point five is a terminating decimal. Others go on forever in a pattern, which we call recurring. For example, one third is a recurring decimal.

faq.q: What is the difference between rational and real numbers?
faq.a: Rational numbers are those that can be written as a simple fraction. Real numbers include all rational numbers plus any irrational numbers, like pi. You might also ask, 'What is the difference between ℚ and ℝ?' or 'Are all rational numbers real numbers?'
asks: What is the relationship between ℚ and ℝ?
Do all rational numbers count as real numbers?

faq.q: Does zero belong to the set of integers?
faq.a: Yes, zero is definitely an integer. Integers include all whole numbers, both positive and negative. You could also ask, 'Is 0 in ℤ?' or 'Are whole numbers included in integers?'

faq.q: How do I check if a decimal is terminating?
faq.a: A decimal terminates if it has a finite number of digits after the point. For example, one quarter is zero point two five, which stops. You might also ask, 'What makes a decimal terminate?' or 'Is 0.75 terminating?'
asks: How do I know if a decimal stops?

faq.q: Can negative numbers be natural numbers?
faq.a: No, natural numbers are always positive counting numbers starting from one. Negative numbers belong to the set of integers. You might also ask, 'Are negative numbers natural numbers?' or 'What is the smallest natural number?'

faq.q: If a number is a fraction, is it always rational?
faq.a: Yes, any number that can be written as a fraction of two integers is rational. This is the definition of a rational number. You could also ask, 'Is every fraction rational?' or 'What is the set of all fractions?'
asks: Does being a fraction mean it is rational?

facts: Natural numbers are the counting numbers: 1, 2, 3, and so on.
Integers include all whole numbers, positive, negative, and zero.
Rational numbers can always be written as a fraction of two integers.
Terminating decimals are a type of rational number.
Pi, pi, is a famous example of an irrational number.

quiz.say: Which set contains the number three?
quiz.show: 3 is in ℕ, ℤ, ℚ, and ℝ.
quiz.why: The natural numbers are the smallest set that includes three, but it is also in the other three sets.

wrong.1: This is tempting because integers include all natural numbers, but ℕ is the most specific correct answer here.
wrong.2: This is tempting because all natural numbers are rational, but ℕ is the most specific correct answer.
wrong.3: This is tempting because all numbers are real, but ℕ is the most specific correct answer.

quiz.say: Which set contains the number negative five?
quiz.show: -5 is in ℤ, ℚ, and ℝ.
quiz.why: Negative five is a whole number, so it belongs to the integers, and also the rational and real numbers.

wrong.0: This is tempting because it is a real number, but ℤ is a more specific correct classification.
wrong.2: Natural numbers cannot be negative, so this option is incorrect.
wrong.3: While it is rational, the set of integers is the most specific correct set listed here.

quiz.say: Which set contains the number zero point seven five?
quiz.why: Because zero point seven five is a terminating decimal, it can be written as the fraction three over four, so it is rational.

wrong.0: Zero point seven five is not a whole number, so it cannot be an integer.
wrong.1: Natural numbers must be positive whole numbers, which zero point seven five is not.
wrong.2: While it is a real number, the set of rational numbers is the most specific correct classification here.
